name: Cuba

facts.religion: Catholic and Afro-Cuban Santería, many non-religious

snapshot: A US oil blockade after the fall of Maduro collapsed Cuba's power grid several times in 2026, leaving millions in the dark and sparking rare protests.
culture: Cuban music, from son and rumba to the Buena Vista Social Club and reggaeton, has shaped Latin sound worldwide. Santería blends Yoruba gods with Catholic saints. Baseball, classic American cars, cigars, and the faded colonial grandeur of Old Havana are global symbols of the island. Its ballet and medical schools are internationally respected.
society: The 1959 revolution built free healthcare and education, but the economy has collapsed since the pandemic, with food, medicine and fuel shortages. More than a tenth of the population has emigrated since 2021. Cuba depended on Venezuelan oil, so the US move against Caracas hit it hard. Small private businesses have been allowed since 2021.
situation: For 65 years Cuba's communist government has survived the US embargo by finding patrons: first the Soviet Union, then Hugo Chávez's Venezuela, which sent it subsidised oil in exchange for doctors. In January 2026, US forces seized Venezuela's Nicolás Maduro, and Cuba's lifeline was cut overnight.

Trump halted Venezuelan oil shipments to the island and threatened tariffs on any country that supplied it. By mid-March, President Miguel Díaz-Canel said Cuba had received no imported oil for three months and was running on 40 percent of the fuel it needed; tens of thousands of surgeries were postponed (AP via PBS). On 16 March the national grid collapsed completely, the third nationwide failure in a month, leaving 10 million people in darkness (NPR via Michigan Public). Rare protests broke out; in Morón, demonstrators damaged a Communist Party office. Trump mused about a "friendly takeover of Cuba," adding that "it may not be a friendly takeover," and his administration demanded the release of political prisoners and economic liberalisation in exchange for lifting sanctions. Díaz-Canel confirmed for the first time that Havana was negotiating with Washington, with Secretary of State Marco Rubio, a Cuban-American, leading for the US (Reuters via Atlas). Cuba has since announced concessions, but the economy remains in free fall, and more than a million Cubans have emigrated since 2021.
power: A one-party communist state. The Communist Party is constitutionally "the superior leading force of society." The National Assembly, with candidates vetted by the party, elects the president for up to two five-year terms. Raúl Castro, 95, retains influence behind the scenes.
holders: President Miguel Díaz-Canel, also first secretary of the Communist Party; Prime Minister Manuel Marrero.
